def-qftx-super-poincare-algebra-4d:
## Definition

Use the complex field $\mathbb C$ with conjugation $z\mapsto\overline z$. Fix an integer $N\ge1$. Let $S=\mathbb C^2$ and let $\dot S=\overline S$ be its conjugate vector space, with dotted basis labels. In the chosen bases put $\epsilon_{12}=\epsilon_{\dot1\dot2}=1$ and $\epsilon_{21}=\epsilon_{\dot2\dot1}=-1$, with zero diagonal. Write $\mathfrak{sl}(S)$ and $\mathfrak{sl}(\dot S)$ for the traceless complex $2\times2$ matrices. The complex even space is

$$\mathfrak g_{\bar0}=\bigl(\mathfrak{sl}(S)\oplus\mathfrak{sl}(\dot S)\bigr)\oplus V\oplus C_N,\qquad V=S\otimes\dot S,\qquad C_N=\Lambda^2\mathbb C^N\oplus\overline{\Lambda^2\mathbb C^N}.$$

Write $T_{\alpha\dot\beta}$ for the basis of $V$. The central space $C_N$ has generators $Z^{IJ}$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}$ for $1\le I<J\le N$, extended by antisymmetry in the flavor indices and with zero diagonal. The complex odd space is

$$\mathfrak g_{\bar1}=(S\otimes\mathbb C^N)\oplus(\dot S\otimes(\mathbb C^N)^*),$$

with basis $Q^I_\alpha$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}$. A homogeneous vector has parity $|x|\in\{0,1\}$. The bracket is complex-bilinear, preserves parity, and obeys $[x,y]=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[y,x]$. Its complete nonzero table, apart from the graded-skew consequences, is

$$[ (A,B),(A',B') ]=([A,A'],[B,B']),\qquad [(A,B),T]= (A\otimes I+I\otimes B)T,$$

$$[(A,B),Q^I_\alpha]=A_\alpha{}^\gamma Q^I_\gamma,\qquad [(A,B),\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}]=B_{\dot\alpha}{}^{\dot\gamma}\bar Q_{\dot\gamma I},$$

$$\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\delta^I{}_J T_{\alpha\dot\beta},\qquad \{Q^I_\alpha,Q^J_\beta\}=2\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}Z^{IJ},\qquad \{\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I},\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=2\epsilon_{\dot\alpha\dot\beta}\bar Z_{IJ}.$$

All other brackets vanish: $V$ and $C_N$ are abelian, $C_N$ is central, and $V$ brackets trivially with the odd space. The two antisymmetric factors in each equal-chirality odd bracket make that bracket symmetric in the combined spinor-flavor labels. The Lie-superalgebra and real-form properties are established by the local Jacobi result.

Define a conjugate-linear involution $*$ on the generators by

$$ (A,B)^*=(-\overline B,-\overline A),\quad Q^I_\alpha{}^*=\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I},\quad \bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}{}^*=Q^I_\alpha,\quad T_{\alpha\dot\beta}^*=T_{\beta\dot\alpha},\quad (Z^{IJ})^*=\bar Z_{IJ},\quad (\bar Z_{IJ})^*=Z^{IJ}.$$

It uses the operator-adjoint convention $[x,y]^*=-(-1)^{|x||y|}[x^*,y^*]$. The associated real Lie superalgebra is the fixed space of the conjugate-linear map $\tau(x)=-x^*$ on even elements and $\tau(x)=i x^*$ on odd elements. Its real Lorentz algebra is the fixed diagonal copy of $\mathfrak{sl}(2,\mathbb C)$; its real translation generators are the $\tau$-fixed skew-Hermitian bispinors. Hermitian physical momenta are obtained by multiplying those real translation generators by $-i$ in a unitary representation.

For the metric convention $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, put $\sigma^0=I_2$ and

$$\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad \sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad \bar\sigma^0=I_2,\qquad \bar\sigma^j=-\sigma^j.$$

They obey

$$\sigma^\mu\bar\sigma^\nu+\sigma^\nu\bar\sigma^\mu=-2\eta^{\mu\nu}I_2.$$

Identify the Hermitian bispinor momentum matrix by $T_{\alpha\dot\beta}=\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu$, where $P_\mu=\eta_{\mu\nu}P^\nu$. This fixes the mixed relation as $\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\delta^I{}_J$. In a massive rest fiber $P^\mu=(M,0,0,0)$, so $P_0=-M$ and the mixed anticommutator is $2M\delta_{\alpha\dot\beta}\delta^I{}_J$. Here $N$ counts left Weyl spinors; the scalar central-charge matrix is antisymmetric and therefore vanishes for $N=1$. Tensorial or topological extensions are outside this scalar-central-charge algebra. The convention uses natural units $\hbar=c=1$; translation and central-charge generators have mass dimension one and supercharges have mass dimension one-half.

def-qftx-unitary-super-poincare-represen:
## Definition

Assume Countable Choice. Use the complex Hilbert-space convention that the inner product is linear in its first variable and conjugate-linear in its second. Let $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, $\sigma^0=I_2$, $\sigma^1=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$, $\sigma^2=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix}$, and $\sigma^3=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$. Define $\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)=\{H\in M_2(\mathbb C):H^\dagger=H\}$ and $\Phi:\mathbb R^{1,3}\to\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)$ by $\Phi(x)=-\sigma^\mu x_\mu$. For $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)=\{g\in M_2(\mathbb C):\det g=1\}$, define $\Lambda_g$ by $\Phi(\Lambda_gx)=g\Phi(x)g^\dagger$; the real-linear map $\Phi$ is an isomorphism because $I_2,\sigma^1,\sigma^2,\sigma^3$ form a basis of $\operatorname{Herm}_2(\mathbb C)$, and $\det\Phi(x)=-\eta_{\mu\nu}x^\mu x^\nu$ is preserved. Congruence by $g$ preserves positive-semidefinite Hermitian matrices, so $\Lambda_g$ preserves the chosen future cone. Let $\Lambda_g^\vee$ be the dual action on covectors, $(\Lambda_g^\vee p)(x)=p(\Lambda_g^{-1}x)$. The spin-cover Poincare group is $\mathcal P=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)\ltimes_\Lambda\mathbb R^{1,3}$ with product $(g,a)(h,b)=(gh,a+\Lambda_gb)$.

A **positive unitary super-Poincare representation** in this item is the following data. It includes a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H$, a bounded self-adjoint grading $\Gamma$ with $\Gamma^2=I$, and a strongly continuous unitary representation $U$ of $\mathcal P$ commuting with $\Gamma$. It also includes a regular projection-valued measure $E$ on the Borel subsets of the covector space $(\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ such that

$$U(1,a)=\Phi_E(p\mapsto e^{i p(a)}),\qquad U(g,0)E(B)U(g,0)^*=E(\Lambda_g^\vee B),\qquad E(\mathcal C_+^*)=I,$$

where $\Phi_E$ is the bounded Borel PVM integral, $\mathcal C_+^*=\{p:p^0=-p_0\ge |\vec p|\}$ is the closed future cone in covector coordinates, and $p(a)=p_\mu a^\mu$. The PVM functional calculus makes every translation unitary commute with every $E(B)$. For each coordinate define the self-adjoint translation generator

$$P_\mu=p_\mu(E),\qquad D(P_\mu)=\left\{\psi\in\mathcal H:\int |p_\mu|^2\,dE_\psi(p)<\infty\right\},\qquad E_\psi(B)=\langle E(B)\psi,\psi\rangle.$$

Here $p_\mu(E)$ is the unbounded PVM integral with its truncation domain; the real-valued integral is self-adjoint under Countable Choice. Thus $P^0=\eta^{0\nu}P_\nu$ is nonnegative. The joint PVM is part of the representation data; no joint spectral measure is inferred from formal commutators on a dense domain.

For each $I,\alpha$, the supercharge $Q^I_\alpha$ is a closed densely defined operator on $\mathcal H$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I}=(Q^I_\alpha)^*$ is its actual Hilbert adjoint, with exactly the adjoint domain. The central generators $Z^{IJ}$ and $\bar Z_{IJ}$ are represented by closed densely defined operators with $\bar Z_{IJ}=(Z^{IJ})^*$ as an actual Hilbert adjoint. On a common dense graded linear domain $\mathcal D$, contained in the domains of every generator product in the bracket table, the operator supercommutator is the displayed algebra bracket. In particular,

$$\{Q^I_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=-2\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}P_\mu\delta^I{}_J,\qquad \{Q^I_\alpha,Q^J_\beta\}=2\epsilon_{\alpha\beta}Z^{IJ},\qquad \{\bar Q_{\dot\alpha I},\bar Q_{\dot\beta J}\}=2\epsilon_{\dot\alpha\dot\beta}\bar Z_{IJ}.$$

The domain $\mathcal D$ is invariant under those generators and under $U(\mathcal P)$. The even group acts on the charge domains exactly: for every $g\in\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb C)$, conjugation by $U(g,0)$ sends each closed charge to the corresponding fundamental or dotted spinor transform as an equality of operators, including equality of domains. The central generators transform as Lorentz scalars, commute with translations, and commute on $\mathcal D$ with all supercharges; these relations also include their domain invariance.

For every Borel set $B\subseteq(\mathbb R^{1,3})^*$ and every charge $Q$ or $Q^*$, require the reducing-projection/domain conditions

$$E(B)D(Q)\subseteq D(Q),\qquad Q E(B)\psi=E(B)Q\psi\quad(\psi\in D(Q)),$$

and the same conditions with $Q^*$ in place of $Q$. Require also $\Gamma E(B)=E(B)\Gamma$ for every Borel $B$. In particular this supplies integrated translation covariance with domain invariance; a relation $[P_\mu,Q]=0$ on a common core alone is not substituted for it. A closed graded subspace $K$ is invariant when $U(g,a)K=K$ for all $(g,a)\in\mathcal P$ and each charge and adjoint maps $D(Q)\cap K$ into $K$, with those intersections dense in $K$. The representation is irreducible when its only such invariant subspaces are $\{0\}$ and $\mathcal H$.
thm-qftx-supermultiplet-mass-degeneracy:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal H$ carry an irreducible positive unitary super-Poincare representation with metric $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, future-cone support and the charge-domain reduction conditions stated in its definition. Let $\mathcal C_+^*$ be the closed future cone from the representation definition and define $s:\mathcal C_+^*	o[0,\infty)$ by $s(p)=-\eta^{\mu
u}p_\mu p_
u$. For Borel $A\subseteq[0,\infty)$ define $F(A)=E(\{p\in\mathcal C_+^*:s(p)\in A\})$. Then every supercharge and its adjoint reduce each mass-squared spectral subspace: if $\psi\in D(Q)\cap\operatorname{ran}F(A)$ then $Q\psi\in\operatorname{ran}F(A)$, and the same holds for $Q^*$. Moreover there is a unique $m^2\ge0$ such that $F(A)=I$ when $m^2\in A$ and $F(A)=0$ when $m^2
otin A$. Thus the nonnegative mass $m=\sqrt{m^2}$ is constant throughout the irreducible multiplet. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $m$ has mass dimension one and $m^2$ has mass dimension two. For a nonzero supercharge image, the source and image lie in the same mass spectral sector. No sharp-momentum eigenvector or rest frame is assumed in the full Hilbert space. If an additional group acts unitarily and commutes with the supercharges on their invariant domains, each supercharge also intertwines that group action; no gauge-charge conclusion is asserted without this extra hypothesis.
thm-qftx-n-extended-central-charge-bound:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $N\ge2$. A fixed massive rest representation fiber consists here of a nonzero complex Hilbert space $\mathcal K$, a number $M>0$ with $P^0=MI$ and $P^j=0$, and scalar central charges $Z^{IJ}=z^{IJ}I$, where $Z=(z^{IJ})$ is the complex antisymmetric $N\times N$ matrix in the four-dimensional algebra with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\epsilon_{12}=1$. Suppose the charge operators and their actual Hilbert adjoints have a common dense invariant domain $\mathcal D$ on the fiber and every product in the expanded anticommutators is defined there. Use natural units $\hbar=c=1$, so $M$ and each $z^{IJ}$ have mass dimension one. For $v=(v_1,\ldots,v_N)\in\mathbb C^N$ define $\|v\|_2^2=\sum_I|v_I|^2$ and for $u,v\in\mathbb C^N$ put $u^*Zv=\sum_{I,J}\bar u_Iz^{IJ}v_J$. Define

$$\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\sup_{\|v\|_2=1}\|Zv\|_2.$$

Then $M\ge\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}$. For $N=2$, write $z=z^{12}$, so $Z=\begin{pmatrix}0&z\\-z&0\end{pmatrix}$ and $\|Z\|_{\mathrm{op}}=|z|$. If $z=e^{i\phi}|z|$ (with any $\phi$ when $z=0$), define on $\mathcal D$

$$A:=Q^1_1-e^{i\phi}(Q^2_2)^*,\qquad A^\sharp:=(Q^1_1)^*-e^{-i\phi}Q^2_2.$$

The algebraic anticommutator $AA^\sharp+A^\sharp A$ equals $4(M-|z|)I$ on $\mathcal D$. Here $A^\sharp$ is the displayed combination of the individual actual adjoints; it is not asserted to be the adjoint of an unbounded sum on its maximal domain. If $\mathcal K$ is finite-dimensional, all charge domains equal $\mathcal K$ and $A^\sharp=A^*$, so the formula is the ordinary operator anticommutator. At saturation $M=|z|$, for every $\psi\in\mathcal D$ one has $A\psi=A^\sharp\psi=0$. This is a representation-theoretic fiber statement: it does not assert that the fixed-momentum fiber is a normalizable subspace of the full Hilbert space, or that a state with specified charge exists or is stable.
def-qftx-superspace-grassmann-algebra:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal A=\mathcal A_{\bar0}\oplus\mathcal A_{\bar1}$ be a finite-dimensional $\mathbb Z_2$-graded complex algebra whose homogeneous elements satisfy $ab=(-1)^{|a||b|}ba$, equipped with a conjugate-linear parity-preserving involutive anti-automorphism $a\mapsto a^*$ extending complex conjugation on $\mathbb C$. For the ordered index set $J=\{1,2,3,4\}$, let $\Lambda_4$ be the complex vector space with specified basis $(e_S)_{S\subseteq J}$, including $e_\varnothing=1$. Define
$$ \nu(S,T)=|\{(s,t)\in S\times T:s>t\}|,\qquad e_Se_T=\begin{cases}0,&S\cap T\ne\varnothing,\\(-1)^{\nu(S,T)}e_{S\cup T},&S\cap T=\varnothing.\end{cases} $$
Put $\xi_1=\theta^1=e_{\{1\}}$, $\xi_2=\theta^2=e_{\{2\}}$, $\xi_3=\bar\theta^{\dot1}=e_{\{3\}}$, and $\xi_4=\bar\theta^{\dot2}=e_{\{4\}}$. Then each $\xi_i$ is odd, $\xi_i^2=0$, and $\xi_i\xi_j=-\xi_j\xi_i$ for $i\ne j$. Give $\Lambda_4$ the grading $|e_S|=|S|\bmod2$. The superspace coefficient vector space is $\mathcal A\otimes_\mathbb C\Lambda_4$ with total parity and graded-tensor multiplication
$$ (a\otimes e_S)(b\otimes e_T)=(-1)^{|S||b|}(ab)\otimes(e_Se_T) $$
for homogeneous $a,b$. On the basis, the left derivative removes $i$ with sign $(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s<i\}|}$ and the right derivative removes $i$ with sign $(-1)^{|\{s\in S:s>i\}|}$ when $i\in S$, and both give zero when $i\notin S$. On a coefficient-left homogeneous tensor $a\otimes e_S$, define $\partial^L_{\xi_i}(a\otimes e_S)=(-1)^{|a|}a\otimes\partial^L_{\xi_i}e_S$ and $\partial^R_{\xi_i}(a\otimes e_S)=a\otimes\partial^R_{\xi_i}e_S$; in particular both vanish on $a\otimes1$. The algebra axioms and derivative rules below are verified in the local well-definedness result. Complex conjugation on this coefficient algebra extends the given operation on $\mathcal A$ by $i^*=-i$, $(\theta^\alpha)^*=\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$, $(\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha})^*=\theta^\alpha$, and $(uv)^*=v^*u^*$. In the coefficient-left tensor notation this means $(a\otimes e_S)^*=(-1)^{|a||S|}a^*\otimes e_S^*$, where $e_S^*$ is obtained by reversing the ordered generator word for $e_S$ and applying the stated generator conjugation.

For each $i\in J$, the left derivative $\partial^L_{\xi_i}$ is the unique odd derivation of the graded tensor algebra that vanishes on $\mathcal A$ and has $\partial^L_{\xi_i}\xi_j=\delta_{ij}$; on homogeneous $u,v$ it obeys
$$ \partial^L_{\xi_i}(uv)=(\partial^L_{\xi_i}u)v+(-1)^{|u|}u(\partial^L_{\xi_i}v). $$
The right derivative $\partial^R_{\xi_i}$ is the unique right odd derivation vanishing on $\mathcal A$ with $\partial^R_{\xi_i}\xi_j=\delta_{ij}$ and
$$ \partial^R_{\xi_i}(uv)=(-1)^{|v|}(\partial^R_{\xi_i}u)v+u(\partial^R_{\xi_i}v). $$
For one generator, write a polynomial uniquely with that generator on the left as $f=f_0+\xi_i f_1$, with $f_0,f_1$ independent of $\xi_i$, and define its Berezin integral by the complex-linear coefficient-extraction rule $\int d\xi_i\,f=f_1$. Thus $\int d\xi_i\,1=0$ and $\int d\xi_i\,\xi_i=1$. Fix the ordered measures
$$ \int d^2\theta:=\int d\theta^2\,d\theta^1,\qquad \int d^2\bar\theta:=\int d\bar\theta^{\dot2}\,d\bar\theta^{\dot1},\qquad \int d^4\theta:=\int d\bar\theta^{\dot2}\,d\bar\theta^{\dot1}\,d\theta^2\,d\theta^1. $$
With this order, $\int d^4\theta$ extracts the coefficient of $\theta^1\theta^2\bar\theta^{\dot1}\bar\theta^{\dot2}$. For superspace coordinates $x=(x^0,x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^{1,3}$ in natural units $\hbar=c=1$, assign mass dimensions $[x^\mu]=-1$, $[\theta^\alpha]=[\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}]=-\tfrac12$, $[d\theta^\alpha]=[d\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}]=\tfrac12$, and hence $[d^2\theta]=[d^2\bar\theta]=1$ and $[d^4\theta]=2$. These are formal engineering dimensions; no physical model or empirical unit convention is asserted.

def-qftx-n1-chiral-superfield:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal A=\mathcal A_{\bar0}\oplus\mathcal A_{\bar1}$ be the finite-dimensional supercommutative complex coefficient algebra, and let $\Lambda_4$ have ordered generators $\theta^1,\theta^2,\bar\theta^{\dot1},\bar\theta^{\dot2}$ and the product, parity, derivatives and conjugation specified in the four-dimensional superspace Grassmann algebra. Let $\mathscr S=C^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3},\mathcal A\otimes\Lambda_4)$ be the space of smooth coefficient functions; $\partial_\mu$ differentiates the real coordinate $x^\mu$ and acts trivially on the finite Grassmann basis. Use the mostly-plus metric and the matrices $\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}$ specified by the four-dimensional super-Poincare algebra. A **chiral superfield** is an even element $\Phi\in\mathscr S$ satisfying the two equations

$$\bar D_{\dot\alpha}\Phi=0,\qquad \bar D_{\dot\alpha}:=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}-i\sum_{\alpha,\mu}\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu,\quad \dot\alpha\in\{\dot1,\dot2\}.$$

Define the nilpotent coordinate shift $\Delta y^\mu=i\sum_{\alpha,\dot\alpha}\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$ and $y^\mu=x^\mu+\Delta y^\mu$. For a smooth coefficient function $f$, $f(y)$ means the finite Taylor substitution $\sum_{k=0}^{2}(\Delta y^{\mu_1}\cdots\Delta y^{\mu_k}/k!)\,\partial_{\mu_1}\cdots\partial_{\mu_k}f(x)$, with the $k=0$ term equal to $f(x)$ and repeated spacetime indices summed; higher terms vanish in $\Lambda_4$. The chiral components are the unique smooth coefficient functions $A,F\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3},\mathcal A_{\bar0})$ and $\psi_1,\psi_2\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^{1,3},\mathcal A_{\bar1})$ in

$$\Phi(y,\theta)=A(y)+\theta^1\psi_1(y)+\theta^2\psi_2(y)+\theta^1\theta^2F(y).$$

The total parity of every term is even. Define the supersymmetry generators on $\mathscr S$ by

$$Q_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}-i\sum_{\mu,\dot\alpha}\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu,\qquad \bar Q_{\dot\alpha}=-\partial^L_{\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}}+i\sum_{\mu,\alpha}\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\partial_\mu.$$

For external odd constant parameters $\epsilon^\alpha,\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}$ that anticommute with the odd generators and coefficient algebra, set $\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}\Phi=\sum_\alpha\epsilon^\alpha Q_\alpha\Phi+\sum_{\dot\alpha}\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}\Phi$. The component transformation is, by definition, the unique ordered-basis coefficient tuple of this transformed superfield in the displayed $y,\theta$ expansion. The space of fields is classical and smooth, so these differential operations have common domain $\mathscr S$; no quantum-field operator domain or field equation is assumed. In natural units $[x^\mu]=-1$ and $[\theta]=[\bar\theta]=-\tfrac12$. If $[\Phi]=d$ is assigned, the formal component dimensions are $[A]=d$, $[\psi_\alpha]=d+\tfrac12$, and $[F]=d+1$; no value of $d$ is fixed. In the same natural-unit convention, $D_\alpha$, $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$, $Q_\alpha$ and $\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}$ have mass dimension $+\tfrac12$, while $[\epsilon^\alpha]=[\bar\epsilon^{\dot\alpha}]=-\tfrac12$, so $\delta_{\epsilon,\bar\epsilon}$ is dimensionless.
lem-qftx-n1-chiral-superspace-identities:
## Statement

For the smooth finite Grassmann-valued superspace and left-derivative conventions in the chiral-superfield definition, the covariant derivatives obey $\{D_\alpha,D_\beta\}=0$, $\{\bar D_{\dot\alpha},\bar D_{\dot\beta}\}=0$, and $\{D_\alpha,\bar D_{\dot\beta}\}=-2i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\beta}\partial_\mu$, where $D_\alpha=\partial^L_{\theta^\alpha}+i\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\gamma}\bar\theta^{\dot\gamma}\partial_\mu$ and $\bar D_{\dot\beta}$ is as defined there. The kernel of both $\bar D_{\dot\alpha}$ consists exactly of the fields independent of $\bar\theta$ when written in the nilpotently shifted coordinate $y^\mu=x^\mu+i\theta^\alpha\sigma^\mu_{\alpha\dot\alpha}\bar\theta^{\dot\alpha}$; hence every chiral field has the unique four-component expansion stated there. The supercharges $Q_\alpha,\bar Q_{\dot\alpha}$ anticommute with each $\bar D_{\dot\beta}$, so the defined supersymmetry transformation preserves chirality and induces a unique smooth component transformation.
lem-qftx-supercharge-positive-energy-pai:
## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$ be a complex Hilbert space with grading operator $\Gamma=+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $\Gamma=-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$. Let $Q$ be a densely defined self-adjoint operator with domain invariant under $\Gamma$ and $Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma Q\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(Q)$. Set $H=Q^2$ on the composition domain $D(H)=\{\psi\in D(Q):Q\psi\in D(Q)\}$. For each $\lambda>0$, let $E_\lambda=\{\psi\in D(H):H\psi=\lambda\psi\}$ be finite-dimensional, and put $E_\lambda^\pm=E_\lambda\cap\mathcal H^\pm$. Then $Q$ maps $E_\lambda$ into itself, and

$$U_\lambda:=(Q/\sqrt{\lambda})|_{E_\lambda^+}:E_\lambda^+\longrightarrow E_\lambda^-$$

is a unitary isomorphism, with inverse $(Q/\sqrt{\lambda})|_{E_\lambda^-}$. In particular $\dim E_\lambda^+=\dim E_\lambda^-$. Also $Q\psi=0$ for every zero-energy vector $\psi\in\ker H$. No discrete spectrum or finite-multiplicity assumption is made about energies other than the selected $\lambda$.
def-qftx-graded-trace-class-index-data:
## Definition

A **pure-point graded trace-class index datum** consists of a complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathcal H^+\oplus\mathcal H^-$, its grading operator $\Gamma$ equal to $+I$ on $\mathcal H^+$ and $-I$ on $\mathcal H^-$, and a densely defined self-adjoint operator $Q$ such that $D(Q)$ is invariant under $\Gamma$ and $Q\Gamma\psi=-\Gamma Q\psi$ for every $\psi\in D(Q)$. Set $H=Q^2$ on $D(H)=\{\psi\in D(Q):Q\psi\in D(Q)\}$ and require this composition operator to be nonnegative and self-adjoint. Assume $H$ has the orthogonal pure-point decomposition

$$\mathcal H=\mathcal H_0^+\oplus\mathcal H_0^-\oplus\widehat{\bigoplus}_{\lambda\in\Sigma}(\mathcal H_\lambda^+\oplus\mathcal H_\lambda^-),$$

where $\Sigma\subset(0,\infty)$ is a supplied countable set of distinct eigenvalues, $\mathcal H_0^\pm=\ker H\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ are finite-dimensional, and $\mathcal H_\lambda^\pm=\ker(H-\lambda I)\cap\mathcal H^\pm$ are finite-dimensional eigenspaces contained in $D(H)$. Supply orthonormal bases of these subspaces whose union $E=E^+\sqcup E^-$ is a Hilbert basis of $\mathcal H$ compatible with energy and parity. Assume Countable Choice as used by the imported Hilbert-space, adjoint and trace-class definitions. The local positive-energy-pairing lemma derives, rather than assumes, the unitary map $Q/\sqrt\lambda:\mathcal H_\lambda^+\to\mathcal H_\lambda^-$ and equality of their finite dimensions.

For each real $\beta>0$, a bounded diagonal operator $T_\beta$ is supplied as part of the data, with $T_\beta e=e^{-\beta\lambda}e$ on $E_\lambda^+\cup E_\lambda^-$ and $T_\beta e=e$ on $E_0^+\cup E_0^-$. Require $T_\beta$ to be trace class for every $\beta>0$; it is denoted $e^{-\beta H}$. Its graded heat supertrace, called the **Witten index at parameter $\beta$** in this data class, is

$$W(\beta):=\sum_{e\in E^+}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle-\sum_{e\in E^-}\langle T_\beta e,e\rangle,$$

where each family sum is in the finite-subset sense for absolutely summable scalar families. The supplied trace-class Hilbert-basis definition makes these sums absolutely convergent. Here $\beta$ is only a positive real mathematical parameter and has no assigned physical units or temperature interpretation. The index datum is discrete: it contains no continuous spectral subspace or continuum regularization prescription, and makes no physical model identification.
thm-qftx-witten-index-beta-independence:
## Statement

For every pure-point graded trace-class index datum with positive-energy blocks paired by the unitary maps $U_\lambda=Q/\sqrt\lambda$ proved from its supercharge data, the absolutely convergent supertrace satisfies

$$W(\beta)=m_0^+-m_0^-\qquad\text{for every }\beta>0.$$

Thus it is independent of $\beta$ and equals the even-minus-odd dimension of the zero-energy subspace. This is a conditional mathematical statement for the discrete trace-class data in the definition; it asserts no continuum cancellation, regularized trace identity, or physical index formula.
